Looping in a couple quick notes from the runtime side:

- For the 500-concurrency soak, we should define two buckets: short chat-like prompts (avg 64 tokens) and long-document prompts (avg 512 tokens). The cost/latency profile differs significantly; we'll give both buckets 60/40 traffic split by default unless you want different.
- We'll enable KV-prefix caching for repeated prompt prefixes (provide the prefix samples in prompts_fixtures.md).
- Routing fallback: if primary model reaches concurrency throttling, traffic will failover to quantized variant in the same region (no cold start). That means you should expect a slight quality delta; good to include a short eval prompt set to check regression.

I can run the load job from Redwood on Friday morning. If FinOps wants to run it from your runner, please send the NAT IP range and we'll white-list.

-rishi
